description: Ground-truth vulnerability list for the Pool.sol eval fixture. A finding 'counts' as matching one of these only if it identifies the same location AND the same underlying issue — a correct category with the wrong location, or a vague restatement of the code without the specific mechanism, does not count as a match. Use with evals/evals.json eval #2 and EVAL-METHODOLOGY.md's Layer 3 scoring.

vulnerabilities.description: External calls (tIn.transferFrom, tOut.transfer) happen before reserveA/reserveB are updated — checks-effects-interactions violation. A malicious or non-standard token (e.g. one with an ERC-777-style hook, or simply a reentrant fallback via tOut.transfer to a contract) can re-enter swap() while reserves still reflect the pre-swap state, manipulating the price used by the reentrant call.
vulnerabilities.why_planted: The single most severe, most classic EVM finding — tests whether the audit actually traces call order rather than pattern-matching on function names.

verified.method: Reviewed against checks-effects-interactions ordering by inspection of the actual call sequence in swap() (external calls at lines 60-61 precede state writes at lines 63-69) — not executed against a live deployment, but the ordering itself is directly readable and unambiguous, which is what 'verified' means for a hand-crafted fixture per EVAL-METHODOLOGY.md's Verified-tier discussion.

fail_to_pass.description: A malicious ERC-20-like token used as tokenB has a transfer() override that re-enters Pool.swap() once, mid-call, before the legitimate swap's reserve update. The test checks the REAL invariant — that the pool's actual token balance never drops below reserveA+reserveB after any sequence of calls — not merely 'did a revert happen', per the SWE-ABS lesson that shallow revert-only tests let wrong fixes pass.
fail_to_pass.expected_before_fix: FAILS — reentrant swap() call executes against stale reserves, and the invariant assertions catch the resulting reserve/balance mismatch even if no explicit revert occurred anywhere in the call chain.
fail_to_pass.expected_after_fix: PASSES once swap() is rewritten checks-effects-interactions-correctly (state updated before external calls) or gains a reentrancy guard — the reentrant call then either reverts (nonReentrant) or operates against already-updated, consistent reserves.

vulnerabilities.pass_to_pass: The fixture's own basic addLiquidity()/swap() happy-path behavior (non-malicious tokens, single-call swaps) must continue to produce the correct amountOut per the constant-product formula after any reentrancy fix — a fix that breaks normal swaps to stop the exploit (e.g. blocking all external calls) is not an acceptable fix.

vulnerabilities.location: swap(), line 49 signature — no minAmountOut parameter
vulnerabilities.description: swap() computes amountOut from live reserves with no caller-supplied minimum-acceptable-output check, so any swap can be sandwiched (frontrun to move the price unfavorably, then backrun) with no way for the caller to bound their slippage.
vulnerabilities.why_planted: Tests whether MEV/slippage-protection is checked as its own category, not folded generically into 'input validation'.

vulnerabilities.description: No minimum-liquidity lock on the first deposit. The first LP can deposit a trivial amount, then a direct token donation to the pool (transfer without calling addLiquidity) before a second LP's deposit can manipulate the effective share price the second LP receives, since lpMinted for subsequent deposits is calculated from reserveA which the direct donation inflated without minting corresponding LP shares.
vulnerabilities.why_planted: Tests whether the audit goes beyond the single-function view and reasons about a multi-step economic attack, per Phase 6's composed-exploit-chain guidance in agency-audit-methodology.md.

vulnerabilities.description: Raw .transferFrom()/.transfer() calls, not SafeERC20, and no check of the boolean return value — a non-standard ERC-20 that returns false instead of reverting on failure would silently fail to move tokens while the function proceeds as if the transfer succeeded.
vulnerabilities.why_planted: A specific, checklist-named category (references/audit-checklist.md 'Unchecked external calls' / 'Unchecked ERC-20 return values') — tests whether the checklist is actually applied line-by-line, not just the headline categories.

vulnerabilities.location: addLiquidity() and swap(), no zero-amount guard
vulnerabilities.description: Neither function rejects a zero amountA/amountB/amountIn — a no-op call still emits a misleading event and (for addLiquidity with totalLp==0) could mint zero LP tokens in a way that leaves totalLp==0 unexpectedly if amountA is also zero, an edge case not otherwise guarded.
vulnerabilities.why_planted: A low-severity, easy-to-miss boundary-value case — tests recall on findings that don't jump out as dramatic.

not_a_vulnerability_but_might_be_flagged.note: Access control is intentionally NOT a finding here — there's no admin/privileged role in this fixture, so an audit that reports a generic 'access control' finding without a specific unauthorized-access scenario is a false positive, not a genuine miss on this fixture's part.
